title: Independently verify E8 odd-field spans with dyadic certificates (no new κ)
body:
Independently corroborates PR6198's S1/S2/S3prime/W2 over every field of characteristic != 2. Adds 6,595 exact row-splitting certificates, 120 explicit isometries and 28,800 root-image checks. No new κ; the selected bound and all five inherited framework assumptions are unchanged.

New relative to Nick Petalas's determinant/reflection-orbit proof: lattice-based root reconstruction, integer-product checking of E=CA, E[:,J]=I and A=A[:,J]E over Z[1/2], and explicit coverage of 28 dependent neighbor pairs (56 extra witnesses). A characteristic-three example exposes a singular anchor Gram matrix while the claimed complement still has rank six. No predecessor executable is imported.

Pins: base a5bff3bf133e482541c09eba4e773884bdb2b1b7; PR6198 head 2a804fcb32f46d66018185194b55f1f2b217523d. Four PR2819 inputs are pinned in SOURCES.json; the audited proof is retained verbatim with SHA256/Git-blob binding. Published commit 0fd1086e41214eff62db2b498728388848fce2d7 has complete tree 2ece3c566dc36d908b6adde829822cc070f3dbcd, identical to the tested local tree.

Reproduce (Python 3.12, standard library):
`python3.12 -I -W error -B research/e8-dyadic-span-audit/verify.py`
Expected: PASS_E8_DYADIC_SPAN_AUDIT, 6595 certificates, 120 transports, 28800 images.

Executed: all four registered commands in normal/optimized Python; full decompressed certificate regeneration; 13 internal rejection controls; four actual certificate corruptions and five source corruptions; metadata, committed bytes/modes/source ancestry; official export integrity and both Git-free read-only replays with unchanged bytes/modes. Remote branch was fetched and its complete tree compared exactly. No hosted CI pass is claimed.

Scope: finite exact certificates plus a written all-field argument, not a proof-assistant theorem or full rank-nine classification. Remaining pinning/sign/SAT and physical-supplier obligations are open. OS track 84; bounded overlap checks and local claim/result are in TASK.json (Discussion posting unavailable).

Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit Nick Petalas/PR6198, DreamingOfClouds/PR2819/2784, CubeJerry/PR3095 and conorholds/PR3755; Apache-2.0. The predecessor retains the field-range theorem.

[Proof, evidence and limitations](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/0fd1086e41214eff62db2b498728388848fce2d7/research/e8-dyadic-span-audit).
